key_insight: GRPO is most rollout-efficient when prompts are selected in Fisher--Rao arc-length coordinates, where pass-rate uncertainty becomes Gaussian and informative groups can be targeted directly.
engineering_relevance: The paper turns prompt sampling into a drop-in curriculum mechanism, reducing wasted rollouts while improving GRPO accuracy on math reasoning benchmarks across multiple backbones.
method: Reparameterize Bernoulli pass rates by arc length ψ = arcsin√p on the Fisher--Rao manifold.
Use a Gaussian curriculum in arc length, with center and width tied in closed form to the target objective (pass@k or pass^k).
Implement ARCUS: Kalman-filter prompt tracking, objective-matched Gaussian scoring, and retention only of informative groups for the standard GRPO update.
evidence_signal: Across six mathematical reasoning benchmarks and three backbones, ARCUS improves average GRPO accuracy by 2.8–2.9 points, beats dynamic sampling by 1.1–1.2 points, and uses 48–57% fewer rollouts.
watch_item: The method depends on accurate online estimation of prompt pass rates in arc length, so miscalibrated uncertainty tracking or nonstationary prompt behavior could reduce its gains.
paper_title: Prompts Live on an Arc: Gaussian Curricula in Fisher--Rao Coordinates for Rollout-Efficient GRPO
